title: Two Eyes in the Mist
story:
The cobblestone streets of Oakhaven were cooler than the workshop, smelling of damp stone and coal smoke. James walked carefully, the brass canister bumping gently against his side with every step. He passed a tall iron lamp that hummed like a sleepy bee. He passed a darkened shop window that held a row of silent boots. He passed a stone archway where the wind whispered of old rain, guiding him deeper into the sleeping town.

Then, the quiet of the night was shattered. James heard it before he saw it—a deep, rhythmic growl that vibrated through the soles of his feet, far heavier than the ticking clocks he had left behind. He pressed his back against the cold brick of a bakery wall, clutching the leather strap tight against his chest. He had never seen a carriage move without horses. He had never felt a sound shake the stones in his ribs. He had never smelled something so fiercely alive yet entirely made of iron.

Rounding the corner came a magnificent, terrifying beast of black metal and gleaming glass. Two brilliant, blinding eyes of yellow light sliced through the Oakhaven mist, throwing long, dancing shadows across the cobblestones. Its four wheels of thick, dark rubber hissed against the damp street as it rolled past, leaving a warm gust of wind in its wake. As the vehicle rumbled by, James caught a sharp, heavy scent—the very same metallic, oily aroma he had smelled on the hillside and seen pooling by the outer fence.

The metal carriage turned another corner, its red taillights fading into the mist like two dying embers. James stood frozen for a moment, listening to the growling sound slowly dissolve back into the silence of the night. He looked up, past the chimney pots and steep slate roofs, to where a great stone dome rose against the starry sky, illuminated by the pale light of the moon. The Grand Library was finally in sight, and the path ahead was clear.
